function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repo.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node 18 image for the app |
| `k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | GitHub Actions that builds the app, runs tests, and pushes a Docker image to GHCR |

> **NOTE** – The repo is assumed to be a simple Express/Node app that listens on port **3000** (adjust if your app uses a different port).

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – Alpine for a small footprint
FROM node:18-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the metadata files first – this keeps the cache happy
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small and includes the latest LTS Node.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a reproducible install.  
> * The container starts with `node app.js` – change if your entry point differs.

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder `k8s/` (or any name you prefer) and add `nodejs-welcome.yaml`:

```yaml
# k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80          # Service port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **What to tweak?**  
> * `image:` – point to the registry you’ll push to (GHCR, Docker Hub, etc.).  
> * `replicas:` – scale as needed.  
> * `service.type:` – change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `ci.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    # Checkout the repo
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    # Set up Node.js
    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    # Install dependencies
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    # Run tests (optional – remove if you don’t have tests)
    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test

    # Build Docker image
    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .

    # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
    - name: Log in to GHCR
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    # Push Docker image
    - name: Push Docker image
      run: |
        docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> **Key points**  
> * The workflow triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * It installs deps, runs tests, builds a Docker image tagged with the commit SHA, logs into GHCR, and pushes the image.  
> * If you prefer Docker Hub, replace the registry and login step accordingly.

---

## 4. Add, Commit & Push

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo (if you haven’t already)
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome

# 2. Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# 3. Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"

# 4. Push
git push origin main
```

> **After pushing**  
> * The GitHub Actions workflow will run automatically.  
> * Once the image is pushed to GHCR, you can deploy it to any Kubernetes cluster using `kubectl apply -f k8s/nodejs-welcome.yaml`.

---

### Quick sanity check

```bash
# Verify Dockerfile builds locally
docker build -t nodejs-welcome-test .

# Run the container
docker run -p 3000:3000 nodejs-welcome-test
```

If the app responds on `http://localhost:3000`, everything is wired correctly.

Happy coding! 🚀
